title: Discharge an extinguisher at a burning bin: pull its pin, aim the horn, squeeze
instruction: Put out the fire in the waste bin with the extinguisher.
context: Fire wardens, security guards (O*NET 33-9032.00) and kitchen staff are taught PASS: pull the pin, aim at the fire, squeeze, sweep. The pin is the step forgotten under stress; squeezing at the wrong place wastes the charge. The instruction does not mention the pin. Unlike TK-PELX9P (place the right extinguisher), TK-CDZ9NC (fit a lockout pin) and TK-4U3MEA (aim an inhaler away from a person), here a blocking pin must come out and the target is picked by a visible fire that moves between lots.
setup: Positions from the robot's view: 'in front' is the distance ahead of the line through the two arm bases, 'left' and 'right' are from the midline halfway between them, heights are above the table top. Extinguisher (fixed): its upright axis 23.0 cm in front and 6.0 cm right. A grey floor stand 100 x 100 x 8 mm; a red painted steel body 80 mm across up to 90 mm high; a steel valve head 40 x 40 x 30 mm (90 to 120 mm high). A black plastic carry handle 80 x 20 x 8 mm sticks out from the head toward the robot (from 2 to 10 cm nearer the robot than the axis, 92 to 100 mm high). Above it a black plastic squeeze lever 125 x 20 x 10 mm (135 to 145 mm high) runs from 2.5 cm beyond the axis to 10 cm toward the robot, hinged 2 cm beyond the axis at 140 mm high, sprung up (0.3 N m per radian); it stops on the handle after 0.33 rad (19 degrees). Under the lever, 5 cm nearer the robot than the axis, a tab 20 mm front to back and 12 mm wide hangs to 123.5 mm high. On the handle there, a black plastic bracket 20 x 52 x 8 mm carries two steel lugs 20 mm front to back either side of the lever (15 to 25 mm left and right of the axis, 100 to 135 mm high), each with a hole 11 mm front to back and 12 mm tall (112 to 124 mm high). Safety pin (loose, steel, 60 g): a rod 10 mm across and 60 mm long lying left to right through both lug holes, under the tab, with a square ring of 5 mm steel (30 mm wide, 37 mm tall, from 12.5 mm below to 24.5 mm above the rod's axis) on its right end, 3 to 6 cm right of the axis. With the pin in, the tab is 1.5 mm above it and the lever moves only a few degrees. Hose and horn: a black rubber hose 14 mm across from the body's far side, 40 mm high, 9 cm long, then a black plastic horn 26 mm across and 5 cm long, its mouth 18 cm beyond the axis; it swivels flat about a vertical axis 27.0 cm in front and 6.0 cm right, up to 57 degrees either way, with damping so it stays where it is left, and starts pointing straight ahead. Bins (loose, painted steel, weighted to 1.5 kg each, 90 x 90 x 100 mm): a red waste bin on fire and a blue recycling bin with a white paper sheet 60 x 45 x 4 mm on top. The fire is rigid painted foam: an orange layer 70 x 70 x 10 mm on the red bin's rim and five tapered flame tongues standing on it, 85, 70, 65, 55 and 50 mm tall (the tallest at the centre, the others about 3 cm from it toward each corner), each an orange square 18 mm across for its lower 45%, then amber 12 mm across for 35%, then yellow 6 mm across. The bins are centred 25 cm from the swivel axis at 40 degrees either side of straight ahead: the left mark 46.2 cm in front and 10.1 cm left, the right mark 46.2 cm in front and 22.1 cm right. Lot A: red waste bin on the left mark, blue bin on the right. Lot B swaps the two bins. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Pass/fail per trial, from the video and a top photo. Discharge: the pin wholly out of both lugs (moved 60 mm or more), the lever squeezed to within 3 degrees of the handle (0.28 rad or more), and the horn's line, seen from above, passing within 40 mm of the red bin's centre ahead of its mouth, all at once for 2 s. 1.0: a discharge happened; the lever was never pressed 0.12 rad (7 degrees) or more while the horn pointed anywhere else; neither bin was moved more than 20 mm; and at the end the lever is let go (back within 3 degrees of up), both grippers are at least 5 mm from the lever, the horn and the pin, and everything has been still for 1.5 s. 0 otherwise, including any press of 0.12 rad or more at the blue bin or at nothing (a part squeeze counts), or with the pin in (it cannot move), pulling the pin and aiming without squeezing, and moving a bin to the horn. Judged over the whole trial. Trials are run on each of lots A and B and averaged.
reset_notes: Put the pin back through both lugs, ring to the robot's right, under the lever's tab; let the lever spring up; turn the horn straight ahead; set the bins on their lot's marks (lot A: red waste bin on the left mark, lot B: on the right). Nothing is consumed (no agent is discharged).
fidelity: Bench scale: an extinguisher 14.5 cm tall, body fixed in its stand (a real one is lifted out), pin 10 mm thick, and a lever needing well under 1 N (tens of N on a real one). The hose is a rigid horn on a damped swivel. Nothing is discharged and the flames never go out: the steps are scored, not a fire; no sweep. Aim is checked from above, at the bin's centre. Lots A and B swap the bins, stopping a fixed swing but not a replay of both.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B); demo: 1.0 in each lot
